answer.rationale: The 18% cost reduction mandate must be met. While the low-cost vendor’s quote satisfies the target (per current situation), switching risks disruption to the no-buffer assembly line (94% utilization). Historical evidence shows the incumbent has responded to benchmarking (memory_c4) and multi-year volume pricing (memory_c6), indicating negotiation can secure the required reduction. This preserves the stable, no-migration integration (memory_c1) critical for the line’s lack of buffer, while the previous successful switch (memory_c2) provides strong leverage. This approach minimizes TCO by avoiding transition costs and maintains current delivery risk levels.
